facts.text: The project is a Python API for AVIS Engine, an autonomous-vehicle simulation platform
The README's Getting Started section launches the simulator and starts its server (section 1) before it connects and controls the vehicle (section 2)
The simulator's documented default server address is 127.0.0.1 and port 25001
config.py sets SIMULATOR_IP to 127.0.0.1 and SIMULATOR_PORT to 25001
AVIS Engine's main class is Car, the object a client instantiates to drive the simulated car
The Car transport is a TCP socket (AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM)
The request is a comma-separated text command with Speed, Steering, ImageStatus, SensorStatus, GetSpeed and SensorAngle fields
connect(server, port) connects the socket and sets a 5.0 s socket timeout
setSpeed stores speed_value, disables image and sensor replies, updates the request and sends it
setSteering stores steering_value, disables image and sensor replies, updates the request and sends it
setSensorAngle stores sensor_angle, disables image and sensor replies, updates the request and sends it
getData requests image, sensor and speed data and parses the <image>, <sensor> and <speed> tags of the reply
getSensors returns the three distance readings as a list [left, middle, right]
getSpeed returns current_speed
getData decodes the reply's <image> payload from base64 and OpenCV into self.image
getImage returns self.image, the image the client stored
stop sets speed and steering to 0, sends the text command 'stop' and closes the socket
The README documents the throttle range as -100 to 100
The README documents the steering range as -100 to 100
The README documents sensor distances in cm
The README documents the current speed in km/h
The README documents getSensors as [left, middle, right] distances in cm and getSpeed as km/h
The example comment calls setSteering a steering angle in degrees
The example sets the angle between sensor rays to 45 degrees, once from the client
The example returns three sensor values and an integer speed in KMH
The README's license section says MIT License and refers to a LICENSE file

determinism.notes: the fake keeps plain attributes and has no random source; the same command sequence gives the same state, while the external simulator's own state depends on its scene and physics

gaps: the fake is an in-process stand-in for Car, not the AVIS Engine simulator: it has no Unity scene, track, traffic, vehicle dynamics, collision or physics and no wall-clock pacing
NOT COVERED: the camera image array returned by Car.getImage(); no capability returns it, and its real base64/OpenCV payload is not modelled
the three distance readings and the speed are placeholders that change only with the throttle, steering and sensor-angle commands; no ray casting or vehicle motion is computed
no socket, <EOF> framing, image decoding or 5.0 s receive timeout: the fake never contacts the documented simulator address 127.0.0.1:25001
the fake's stop only zeroes the commands and records the stop; unlike Car.stop it does not close a connection, and the external simulator is never run or compared with the fake
